competitive_landscape: A dense, mature ferry market (SeaJets, Blue Star, Golden Star) plus superyacht tenders and RIB charters — strong demand proof and partners. The meltemi-driven ride-quality problem is the clearest pain. No foiling incumbent.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II owns the core Cyclades mesh — Mykonos, Paros, Naxos, Ios and the Santorini edge (~62 nm) — plus all tender and villa transfers.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR (H2 2026+) links the Cyclades to Athens/Saronic and Crete on longer Aegean trunks.

precedents.why_it_matters: The Cyclades reproduce the dense short-hop island-transfer pattern at Mediterranean scale and seasonality.

regulatory_note: Greek flag / EU; Hellenic Coast Guard certification; Greek cabotage rules favour EU-flagged vessels. Municipal port funds (Limeniko Tameio) control berths.
seasonality: Sharply seasonal: May–Sep is peak (and meltemi-windy Jul–Aug); winter inter-island demand collapses. The wind constraint is the core operating design point.

sources.label: Greek inter-island ferry operators (SeaJets, Blue Star)

summary: The Cyclades are the world's archetypal island-hopping destination: Mykonos, Paros, Naxos, Ios and Santorini draw millions on a dense ferry network (Blue Star, SeaJets, Golden Star) plus a heavy summer superyacht fleet. Inter-island distances are short and overwhelmingly inside Pioneer II range, while the meltemi-wind chop that makes conventional fast-ferries brutal is exactly where a hydrofoil's ride quality wins.
tagline: The island-hopping mecca of the Aegean — a dense, high-frequency Cyclades ferry and superyacht market.
